newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE white sugar languishes in light trade.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE white sugar languishes in light trade.

text.p: White sugar futures showed a marked reluctance to jolt into life on Wednesday morning as movements on the nearby March/May spread remained thin and turnover light.
Traders said the raws market was unlikely to make much of an impression on London sentiment as some market players were already absent ahead of the two-day holiday.
At 1218 GMT March was up just 30 cents at $304.20 after dipping to a low of $302.50. May was down 40 cents at $304.20 and overall volume was a paltry 79 lots.
Market sources noted the presence of a major fund short in the March whites but said this would be unlikely to have much effect with the contract's expiry so far away.
"It won't become a factor until nearer the expiry...a fund will run it as long as it possibly can and then there's every chance you'll see March/May back to a premium," one trader said.
Technically, March's 10- and 20-day moving averages are starting to converge across the recent tight trading ranges between $303 and $304.
A series of intraday highs just above $305 should act as the contract's first resistance level followed by a couple of highs around $307.
While the shorter five-day momentum indicator has turned lower and is looking to fall below the neutral zero level, the 10-day indicator has just sloped over zero but is levelling off.
In physical news, Wednesday is Syria's deadline to receive bids in its tender to buy 13,000 tonnes of whites and 13,000 tonnes of raws for Dec/Jan. Results are expected on Thursday.
El Salvador tendered to sell 6,250 tonnes of U.S. quota raws for January/February shipment. Bids are to be accepted on an executable order basis against New York's March No.14 contract.
The Paris market saw just 310 lots traded in March, up 40 cents at $303.80.
